hero.title: No need to ask anymore.
hero.subtitle: YoolLive shows the whole trip: where the truck is, where it stopped and why the signal dropped. The driver just marks each step in the app.

chapters.title: A load in a minute
chapters.text: Paste a link from 2GIS, Yandex or Google Maps and the address fills itself in. The cabinet works out the road route and drive time right away.

chapters.title: A driver from one link
chapters.text: You don’t need the driver’s number. Send a link in Telegram: the driver opens it and accepts the load with one tap.

chapters.title: Loaded. With a photo, on the map
chapters.text: The driver marks every step with a button and attaches a photo of the papers. You get a notification, and the map shows where it happened.

chapters.title: You see it moving
chapters.text: The dot in the cabinet moves with the truck: speed, distance driven, time to arrival, even the battery of the driver’s phone.

chapters.title: Stopped, and you know why
chapters.text: Lunch at a chaikhana. The phone turns GPS off by itself to save battery, and the cabinet says: stopped since 12:10. No call needed.

chapters.title: The pass. No signal
chapters.text: On Kamchik the network drops. The app doesn’t lose points, it keeps them on the phone for up to two weeks. The cabinet says “no network” instead of drawing a green dot.

chapters.title: Signal back, track whole
chapters.text: As soon as there’s coverage, every point goes out in one batch. The route fills in with no gaps, as if the signal never dropped.

chapters.title: The client watches on their own
chapters.text: Send the receiver a link. They see the truck on the map without signing up, and stop calling you every half hour.

chapters.title: Delivered
chapters.text: The driver photographs the waybill, you confirm delivery. The trip goes to history with every step, photo and the track.

start.driverText: One screen and one button for the next step. Works without network, saves battery when you stand, tracks location only during a trip. Sign in with Telegram.

items.q: What if the driver loses internet?
items.a: Nothing is lost. The phone keeps route points for up to 14 days and sends them once the network is back. Meanwhile the cabinet shows “no network”, not a stale dot.

items.q: Does the app drain the battery?
items.a: When the truck stands, the app turns GPS off by itself. Location is recorded only while the driver has an active load, and the cabinet shows their phone’s battery.

items.q: What does the client see from the link?
items.a: The load’s name and status, the truck on the map and the route driven so far. No sign-up needed. You can revoke the link at any time.

items.q: Does the driver need to sign up?
items.a: Yes, in the YoolLive app. It takes a minute: sign in with Telegram, Apple or email. If you sent them a load link, the load is accepted right after sign-in.
